title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The handwriting is on the back of a typed sheet. Judging by the neighbouring pages and the ghost text, the typed side is a draft of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Néron models; semi-stable reduction, §7 on the Raynaud extension). The handwritten side is homological algebra serving the 1976 IHES lecture on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex.

Setting:
- C is an abelian category (probably modules over some base ring).
- M_ω is an abelian category of systems indexed by N_0 (most plausibly projective systems (M_n)_{n≥0}, possibly with a limit term ω adjoined).
- σ = φ_{ω N_0} ∘ i_ω : C → M_ω is exact and fully faithful (the 'constant system' functor).
- σ has a right adjoint ψ = K φ_{N_0 ω}, essentially the projective-limit functor, with ψσ ≅ id_C.
- Grothendieck first wrote 'ψ exact', crossed it out, and noted 'σ exact, K exact, but ψ perhaps not exact'. This is exactly the situation of lim versus the constant system.

Argument:
1. Suppose a complex K· in C and a quasi-isomorphism σ(K·) → L·_ω in M_ω are given.
2. Since σ is exact, Rσ K = σ K.
3. One wants Rψ(σK) ≅ R(ψσ)(K) ≅ K. Hence K ≅ Rψ(L_ω): K is recovered as the derived limit of any system quasi-isomorphic to the constant one.
4. He then asks ('?') whether ψ(L_ω) → Rψ(L_ω) is an isomorphism.
5. To answer, he uses the hypercohomology spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = R^qψ(H^p(L_ω)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(Rψ L_ω), sketching the differentials of E_1 and E_2.
6. If R^qψ(H^p(L_ω)) = 0 for q > 0 (Mittag-Leffler-type acyclicity of the cohomology systems), it degenerates, giving H^·(Rψ L_ω) ≅ ψ(H^·(L_ω)).

Second variant:
- A map i(K·) ← L·, truncated/restricted by τ_{ωN_0}, gives K· ≅ R(K_0 φ_ω)(τ_{ωN_0}(L·)).
- The conclusion recorded is that the induced functor D(Mod) → D(M_ω) is fully faithful.

Purpose: recovering a complex (e.g. a de Rham or crystalline-type complex over W or a complete base) as R lim of its reductions mod p^{n+1} or m^{n+1}.
errors: The step Rψ(σK) = R(ψσ)(K) is asserted without justification. Exactness of σ is not enough; one needs σ to send injectives (or a K-injective resolution) to ψ-acyclic objects, or equivalently that σ is fully faithful at the derived level. The last line ('D(Mod) → D(M_ω) pl. fidèle') is essentially equivalent to this step, so the argument is somewhat circular unless this is checked separately. For N-indexed projective systems of modules it does hold: constant systems are lim-acyclic since they satisfy Mittag-Leffler.

The comparison ψ(L) → Rψ(L) is left with a question mark. The spectral sequence condition stated (vanishing of R^qψ on the cohomology objects) controls H(Rψ L) but does not by itself show that ψ applied termwise computes Rψ unless the terms of L are also ψ-acyclic.

ideas.what: Exact fully faithful functor σ: C → M_ω (constant system) with non-exact right adjoint ψ (limit), ψσ ≅ id; recovering K as Rψ of a system quasi-isomorphic to σK
ideas.modern_name: Derived limit R lim and full faithfulness of the constant-diagram functor D(A) → D(A^{N^op})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roos (1961), Jensen; Grothendieck (EGA 0_III §13); Jannsen (1988, continuous étale cohomology)

ideas.what: Spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = R^qψ(H^p L) ⇒ H^{p+q}(Rψ L), degenerating under Mittag-Leffler-type acyclicity
ideas.modern_name: Hypercohomology spectral sequence for R lim / Mittag-Leffler criterion

ideas.what: Recovering a complex over a complete base from truncated/reduced systems, K ≅ R(K_0 φ_ω)(τ L)
ideas.modern_name: Derived completion / R lim of reductions mod p^n (as in crystalline cohomology, Berthelot–Ogus)

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard homological algebra (derived limit of a system quasi-isomorphic to a constant one, Mittag-Leffler degeneration), sketched as an auxiliary lemma for the PD de Rham lecture. Its only incidental interest is that the paper reuses SGA 7 IX drafts.
transcription_corrections: The superscripts read as 'α' in R^α ψ, R^α(ψσ) are the dot/bullet R^· (total derived functor), as the transcription mostly renders.
In the second line the crossed-out word under the curve looks like an aborted 'φ_{ωN_0}', followed by i_ω = σ, as transcribed.
The '[-R-]' at the start of the σ(K·) line is a crossed-out symbol; the line reads 'σ(K·) → L·_ω qu.-isom dans M_ω'.
Grothendieck writes 'mais ψ peut-être pas exact' after crossing out 'ψ exact', so the crossing-out is a correction of an initially wrong assertion.
The typed side of this sheet (visible as ghost text) is a draft of SGA 7 Exposé IX, consistent with the neighbouring pages, which are typed Exposé IX pp. 81–82.
